newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds mixed, look to U.S. jobless report.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds mixed, look to U.S. jobless report.

text.p: Argentine bonds were mixed late Thursday after a session of position squaring ahead of the release of the awaited U.S. unemployment report Friday.
"There is a lot of uncertainty," said one trader at a local bank. That uncertainy kept activity slim.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 slipped 1/8 to 89-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.15 to 127.25.
"There is great uncertainty and a degree of pessimism over Friday's figure," as a strong number could lead the U.S. Federal Reserve to hike rates again, another trader said.

Even if Friday's figure does not spook the market, traders are concerned that Argentine bonds could remain trendless because of the fear that later U.S. data releases will point to rising inflationary pressures.
"I think the upside is limited," said the second trader, as the unemployment report will only get rid off some and not all the uncertainty of more rate hikes.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.35 percent from 6.70 percent.
